BLOCK TEMPLATES Templates are Gutenberg frames stored in WordPress. They use blocks installed by the active theme and plugins. These tools create no block types, PHP files or scripts. List templates before creating, then get-template before editing. Fabrement > Templates in wp-admin opens the same templates; open one there to add, move and edit installed blocks in Gutenberg.
save-template requires mode create, replace or edit. Create needs title and blocks. Replace sends the complete frame, or omits blocks to rename/change metadata only. Edit uses edits and expectedHash from get-template; an outdated hash refuses the write. Preserve unrelated and unknown saved markup. Use exactly one content slot for the page's own content; it may be nested in a group: {name:"fabrement/content-source"}, or core/post-content (which cannot draw a theme PHP file). Slot attributes survive edits. All other blocks follow block-discovery-contract and content-contract: a dynamic PHP renderer alone does not establish save() semantics. ACF data is validated against existing field definitions. Unsafe new or changed HTML/attributes are refused atomically.
THEME PHP SOURCES The slot can draw an existing PHP file from the theme's templates/ folder instead of the page content. That choice is set in wp-admin; get-template shows it as contentSource, read-only, and save-template keeps it. Never send rules or templateId in block attributes; such a block is refused. A template with theme-file rules needs fabrement/content-source as its slot. If the file disappears or throws, the slot falls back to the page's own content without modifying it.
HEADERS AND FOOTERS Create reusable headers/footers with save-synced-pattern and kind header/footer, filled with existing core, ACF or registered blocks. Place them in the frame as {name:"core/block",attributes:{ref:123}}. One shared header edit updates all templates using it. Ordinary blocks can also sit directly in the frame. Use theme/plugin styling or supported Gutenberg design controls.
ASSIGNMENT assign-template-pages with mode add affects only the supplied pageIds. Remove releases those pages. Replace makes pageIds the entire assigned set: use only after inspecting list-template-pages. Every record the call changes must be yours to edit; otherwise nothing is changed. An explicit pick outranks the post type's default. Site-wide assignments — a post type's default, the 404 template, archive views — are made in wp-admin; get-template and list-templates show them. Classic themes with front-page.php and block themes with front-page may override a type default on the homepage. Preview the actual assigned page, not just the saved frame. delete-template is refused while a site-wide assignment points at the template, and while records chose it unless force is explicit; force clears those picks. It does not delete page content or shared header/footer patterns.
save-template publishes the template because it is a shared layout, not a page. Verify an assigned page's frontend and Gutenberg editor. For multilingual templates, read template-translation; never create duplicate originals to translate.
